props.gloss_en: Shmuel: 'and its fat is permitted' -- according to all
candidate: 'its fat' is the fat of the fetus
R' Meir: [the gid prohibition] applies to a fetus

R' Yehuda: it does not apply to a fetus
R' Yehuda: and its fat is permitted
the dispute is about a live nine-month [fetus], and R' Meir went by his view and R' Yehuda by his
candidate, and the stam's conclusion: 'its fat' is the fat of the gid
R' Meir: one scrapes after the gid wherever it is, and cuts its fat from its root
R' Yehuda: one cuts it level with the surface
[Shmuel concedes that] for R' Meir [the gid's fat] is forbidden by rabbinic law -- permitted by the Torah and forbidden by the Rabbis
the baraita: and its fat is permitted
the baraita: and Israel, being holy, treated it as forbidden
the second baraita: one scrapes after the gid wherever it is, and its fat is permitted
Rav: the Torah forbade only its kenokanot (fibres)
Ulla: it [the gid] is wood, and the Torah made one liable for it
Rav Asi: strands in the forbidden fat are forbidden, and one is not liable for them
Rav Asi: [strands] in the kidney are forbidden, and one is not liable for them
the white of the kidney is forbidden (one of Rebbi and R' Chiyya forbids, the other permits)
Rabba would scrape it [the white of the kidney] out; R' Yochanan would scrape it out
R' Asi would cut it off [at the surface]
Shmuel: fat that the flesh covers is permitted
Shmuel: this fat under the loins is forbidden
an animal in its lifetime separates at the joints
Shmuel: fat on the omasum and the reticulum is forbidden, and punished by karet
Shmuel: and this is 'the fat upon the innards'
Shmuel: this fat of the coccyx is forbidden, and punished by karet
Shmuel: and this is 'the fat upon the loins'
Shmuel: strands in the foreleg are forbidden
Rava: did the Merciful One say 'eat blood'? -- [they are forbidden] on account of blood
Rava: if one cut and salted it, even for the pot it is fine
Shmuel: the top of the intestine, for a cubit, requires scraping
Shmuel: and this is 'the fat on the small intestine'
Rav Yehuda: strands in the tail are forbidden
Rav Yehuda: there are five strands in the tail, three on the right and two on the left; the three branch in two each, the two in three each
the practical difference: if one pulls them out while they are warm they come out; if not, one must dig after them
five strands: three on account of fat -- of the spleen, the tail and the kidneys
and two on account of blood -- of the foreleg and of the throat
those on account of blood: if one cuts and salts them, it is fine
those [on account of fat] have no remedy
five membranes: three on account of fat -- of the spleen, the tail and the kidneys
and two on account of blood -- of the testicles and of the brain
Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya was cutting it [the spleen's membrane] from the top only
Levi: go down into it further
Rav: the Torah forbade only what is on the dad (the thick part) alone
Rav Hamnuna's tanna: the membrane on the spleen is forbidden, and one is not liable for it
Levi: what is the case? if what is on the dad -- why is one not liable? rather [the baraita speaks] of all of it
Rav Huna bar Chiyya: if it is taught, it is taught
Rav Hamnuna's tanna: the membrane on the kidney is forbidden, and one is not liable for it
a baraita: one IS liable for it [the membrane on the spleen / on the kidney]
this one [liable] is opposite the dad
that one [not liable] is not opposite the dad
this one [liable] is the upper [membrane]
that one [not liable] is the lower [membrane]
crushed testicles are forbidden (one of Rav Ami and Rav Asi forbids, the other permits)
the one who forbids: since they do not heal, they are a limb from the living
the one who permits: since they do not rot, they have vitality
and the other [who forbids]: that they do not rot is because the air does not reach them
and the other [who permits]: that they do not heal is because weakness has gripped them
R' Yochanan to Rav Shemen bar Abba: but you shall not eat them, on account of 'and do not forsake the teaching of your mother' (Prov 1:8)
Mar bar Rav Ashi: kid's testicles, until thirty days, are permitted without peeling
from then on, if they have seeded they are forbidden
and if they have not seeded they are permitted
how do we know? if they have red streaks they are forbidden; if not, permitted
throughout the Torah Ravina is lenient and Rav Acha stringent, and the halakha is like Ravina leniently -- except these three
raw meat, testicles and neck veins [placed on coals] are permitted -- the lenient view in these three
raw meat, testicles and neck veins [placed on coals] are forbidden -- the stringent view in these three
raw meat that reddened: if one cut and salted it, even for the pot it is fine
if one hung it on a spit, also [fine]: the blood drips out
one says: [the coals] draw it [the blood] out -- and so testicles, and so neck veins
and one says: [the coals] contract it [trapping the blood] -- and so testicles, and so neck veins
a head in the ashes, set on the place of slaughter: the blood drips and it is permitted
set on its sides [with nothing inserted]: [the blood] congeals and it is forbidden
set on its sides with something inserted: permitted
set on its nostrils, with something inserted: permitted
set on its nostrils with nothing inserted: [the blood] drips and it is permitted

deflected_by.gloss_en: ממאי? דילמא רבי יהודה היא, אבל לרבי מאיר מדאורייתא נמי אסיר

refuted_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך: דתניא מחטט אחריו בכל מקום שהוא ושמנו מותר -- מאן שמעת ליה דאית ליה חטיטה? רבי מאיר, וקאמר שמנו מותר (= p_chatita_veshamno_mutar)

supports.gloss_en: כוותיה דעולא מסתברא, דאמר רב ששת אמר רב אסי: חוטין שבחלב אסורין ואין חייבין עליהן -- אלמא חלב אמר רחמנא ולא חוטין, הכא נמי גיד אמר רחמנא ולא קנוקנות
כוותיה דרבי אסי מסתברא, דאמר... שמואל: חלב שהבשר חופה אותו מותר -- אלמא שעל הכסלים אמר רחמנא ולא שבתוך הכסלים, הכא נמי שעל הכליות ולא שבתוך הכליות

frames.gloss_en: חלבו דמאי? -- the fat of what is Shmuel's 'its fat is permitted according to all'?

eliminated_by.gloss_en: הא מיפלג פליגי ביה -- R' Meir forbids the fetus's fat and R' Yehuda permits it (the baraita), and the dispute is about a live nine-month fetus (R' Elazar in R' Oshaya's name, 92b.6), so it cannot be 'according to all'
הא מיפלג פליגי בה -- R' Meir requires scraping and cutting its fat from the root, R' Yehuda cuts it level (the baraita)

rebuffed_by.gloss_en: לעולם חלבו דגיד: Shmuel concedes that for R' Meir it is forbidden only rabbinically, so by Torah law it is permitted according to all (= p_rm_chelev_gid_derabanan)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והאמר רבי אבא אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: האי תרבא דתותי מתני אסיר -- the fat under the loins is covered by flesh and forbidden

answered_by.gloss_en: בהמה בחייה פרוקי מיפרקא -- in life the joints separate, [so it is not fat that the flesh covers] (= p_paroki_mifarka; R' Yochanan recalls the beit midrash saying the same)

objections.gloss_en: משה! מי אמר רחמנא לא תיכול בישרא? -- the strands are meat; did the Torah forbid meat?

answered_by.gloss_en: משה! מי אמר רחמנא אכול דמא? -- they are forbidden for the blood; cut and salt it and it is fine even for the pot (= p_rava_mishum_dama, p_rava_chatcheih_umalcheih)
